direction: Capacity-tightness-aware multiplicative gated rank-power ruin scoring (targeting the 'tight capacity' / eccentric-depot weak regime)

operations.mechanism: Round 4 reached 16.0665, i.e. the frontier is flat (SBS 16.0496 vs VBS-derived gap-over-SBS only 0.56%), so single-digit-percent archetype changes are exhausted and progress must come from regime-targeted reweighting inside the single evolvable hook. The KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the exact score_ruin_nodes math family (rank_power(|removal_savings|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio))) and shows the evolved gated rank-power form beat the Worst-Removal L3-ctrl on both select_64 and blind_120, i.e. the multiplicative-gate + rank-power structure is the verified productive search neighborhood here rather than an untested invention. The KB also flags the failure mode to avoid: naive heavy per-iteration hooks collapse under small budgets (budget-exhaustion early stop), so I keep the hook O(n) vectorized (no per-node re-optimization) and keep the fixed deterministic Regret-2 repair, letting the 2000 ms budget be spent on LNS iterations rather than on scoring. The differentiated ingredient versus the archived solvers is that gate_load and gate_depot are conditioned on observed capacity slack and route depot-distance, which directly attacks the two weakest regimes instead of the already-saturated spatial/demand axes. Postprocess stays 'none' to preserve exact per-iteration attribution of the hook change.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Because the weakest regime reported by the archive is capacity_level=tight (12 instances, vbs_rel_gap_pct = -22.59%) and depot_style=eccentric (-20.35%), the current score_ruin_nodes ranking must be under-serving load-critical customers: it ranks mostly by removal savings, so in tight-capacity instances it repeatedly removes cheap-to-move low-demand nodes and leaves the bin-packing-like capacity structure (and the long depot legs of eccentric instances) untouched. Testable claim: scoring removal priority as a multiplicative gate of (a) normalized removal savings, (b) demand-to-residual-load pressure of the node's route, and (c) a depot-distance gate applied only when the route is far-loaded, combined through a stagnation-driven rank power, will lower mean tour length on dev_24 below the current SBS 16.0496, with the gain concentrated on the tight-capacity and eccentric-depot subsets (predicting subset mean improvement >= 0.05 while uniform-demand/spatial-random subsets stay within noise).
